item.text: {"question_id":"2B.4","answer":"For the 2023 period, the supplied record shows formal humanitarian-law commitments and IHL education, but not demonstrated adoption, resourcing, or enforcement of operational rules of engagement, civilian safeguards, prisoner protections, investigations, discipline, or remedy. China’s Ukraine position and Xi’s April statement called for compliance with IHL, civilian and prisoner protection, humanitarian access, and related safeguards, while the ICRC documented state-linked IHL training and policy discussion (BATCH-0015-E005; BATCH-0016-E001; BATCH-0006-E008). These are policy and capacity signals, not evidence of battlefield implementation. The relevant external conduct supplied is maritime coercion rather than a documented armed conflict: Chinese naval and coast-guard vessels reportedly shadowed, blocked, or endangered Philippine resupply missions, while China characterized the actions as lawful enforcement; the extracts do not establish a violation of the law of armed conflict, but they do leave civilian and personnel-protection practice contested (BATCH-0006-E011; BATCH-0025-E003). The record therefore supports only a limited, qualified finding of formal commitment, with substantial uncertainty about operational safeguards and accountability. General domestic human-rights findings are excluded from the substantive judgment because the supplied extracts do not connect them to battlefield civilian or prisoner
